defectsFound.summary: The browser crawler threw ReferenceError on every call.
defectsFound.mechanism: The runtime-pool integration moved the crawl result variables inside the try block while the return statement stayed below the finally. `pages is not defined`, every call, total failure of the website-audit path.
defectsFound.whyItWasInvisible: check:syntax parses it; the deterministic suite does not cover the browser gate; the pool's own unit tests mock the browser. Only `npm run test:browser` against a real Chromium sees it -- a gate that was recorded as permanently BLOCKED until the previous shift proved Chromium was present all along.

defectsFound.origin: inherited from main, not introduced by #231
defectsFound.summary: A duplicate webhook answered 503 and misstated why.
defectsFound.mechanism: The insert's ON CONFLICT named provider_event_key, correct when that was the only unique index. Migration 101 added a second on the content (provider, event_name, object_type, object_id, payload_hash); a targeted clause does not cover it, so a redelivery of identical content under a new event id raised 23505. The route catches everything and answers 503 verified-webhook-not-durably-persisted -- an outage, and false: the evidence IS persisted, in the row being duplicated. Providers retry 503s and disable endpoints that keep failing, so a duplicate could cost the future events that are not duplicates.
defectsFound.mutation: MONEY-17, killed by a real-PostgreSQL test because which index PostgreSQL raises on cannot be faked

defectsFound.summary: Two mutations shared an id, twice.
defectsFound.mechanism: MONEY-13 and MONEY-14 were both already taken, so a new entry collided twice in a row and the war printed two lines with one id -- ambiguous about which guard survived. Uniqueness and malformedness tests added.

defectsFound.summary: Verified payment evidence accumulated where nobody could see it.
defectsFound.mechanism: The billing webhook route writes a row per verified delivery. Nothing in the tree reads those rows -- claimBillingEvents, finishBillingEvent, billingBacklogSummary and planPaymentReconciliation had no callers anywhere in src, api, scripts, server or worker. Evidence about money arrived, was stored, and was never claimed, retried, timed out, dead-lettered or mentioned to anyone.
defectsFound.fix: Not a reconciliation worker -- there is no provider to reconcile against and a worker that resolves nothing would be machinery pretending to be a capability. The operator health matrix now carries a billing dimension with four states, separating NO_WORKER (nothing has ever claimed a row) from BACKLOG_AGEING (a worker exists and is behind). Those look identical in a pending counter and are not the same fact: one resolves itself, the other never will. Today the real query answers NO_WORKER and the system reports DEGRADED for it.

defectsFound.summary: The deterministic gate changed its answer based on the invoking shell.
defectsFound.mechanism: Most database suites stay in the deterministic set and self-skip when OMNIA_V9_TEST_DATABASE_URL is absent. Exported, they execute there in parallel sharing one database -- the interference run-real-postgres-tests.mjs runs serially to avoid. Symptom: a red property test that passes in isolation.
defectsFound.fix: The runner drops the variable for its children. Identical answer with and without it set.
defectsFound.wrongFirstAttempt: Deriving the deterministic exclusion from realPostgresTestFiles() dropped ~128 genuinely deterministic tests, because that marker matches any file mentioning the variable. The marker is right for PostgreSQL inclusion and wrong for deterministic exclusion. Two build-wiring tests caught it.

defectsFound.summary: Two production-reachable modules were executed by no gate at all.
defectsFound.mechanism: The reachability ratchet asks whether anything CAN call a module. Nothing asked whether anything CHECKS it. Taking the closure of everything the gates import and subtracting it from the production-reachable set found src/database-hygiene-repository.mjs, which DELETES rows on a weekly cron, and src/discovery-runner.mjs, which decides whether discovery may run. The same combination already cost a P0 this shift: the crawler shipped a ReferenceError because its only real gate had been written off.
defectsFound.outcome: Neither module was defective -- both survived every attack unchanged. The defect was that nothing would have noticed if they stopped being right. Both now have suites, and tests/production-coverage-ratchet.test.mjs keeps the uncovered set empty.

survivedAttackUnchanged: Payment lease, against real PostgreSQL: a crashed worker's lease is reclaimable rather than stranded; a preempted worker cannot finish; the attempt cap lands in UNCERTAIN and never promotes money or sets completed_at; RECONCILED without a canonical receipt throws; concurrent claims never hand one event to two workers; RETRYABLE honours its backoff; the backlog summary carries no key or payload.
Overpass pacing: 403, 401, 451, 418 and 404 stop at one call. Only 429, 406 and 504 retry. Retry-After is honoured and an absurd value is clamped to 120s. maxAttempts is clamped to 5.
Browser pool: one process reused, a fresh isolated context per crawl, no slot leaked on launch failure, no double-free on double release, waiters rejected on close rather than hung.
Artifact storage: object backend fail-closed on absent/false/"true"/1/{}/null and open only on literal true; no namespace escape; receipts PRIVATE regardless of input.
observationsNotFixed: The artifact contract's sensitive-metadata-key check is top-level only, so {outer:{api_key}} is accepted. It leaks nothing, because metadata never reaches the plan at all -- the check is a refusal signal, not a redaction. Recorded so nobody later relies on it as a filter.
harnessGapsFixed: The mutation sandbox copied src, tests, scripts, config and migrations but not `api`, so no route could be mutated at all -- a mutation naming one failed with ENOENT rather than reporting a surviving guard. Routes are where admission and enablement checks live. Fixed, and HYG-01 now sabotages the maintenance cron's enablement check.

isStaleSignal compares a signal's age against a maxAgeMs the caller supplies, so a caller can already choose its own answer without discarding anything. Protecting its callers would look like a boundary and enforce nothing. A test asserts they stay editable, with that reason, so nobody tidies them in later.
decisionConsumerSweep.whatWouldReopenIt: A new module that imports a protected decision.
